title: ewa-1998-global-heavyweight

title: ewa-1998-north-american
label: Suicide King

won.source: Not shown in this run's surviving record — Suicide King is already billed North American Cyber Champion entering wnw-8 (5 August 1998), retaining there against Johnny Sledge; Bloodbath '98 (13 September) separately bills Connor Chambers, not Suicide King, as champion entering his own title loss to Lonewolf — see that reign's own note.

how: Unrecorded — first appears as champion at wnw-8, retaining there against Johnny Sledge via moonsault.
note: A third undocumented North American title change in this run's own record, following Connor Chambers and Tommy Grayson (ewa-1998-na-r0005, defended 15 July) — none of the three transitions between these reigns, nor whatever happened between Suicide King and Bloodbath '98's own Chambers billing, is captured in the surviving record. The lineage is recorded exactly as thin as the corpus leaves it, rather than smoothed into a guessed sequence.

title: ewa-1998-north-american
label: Connor Chambers
how: Won a five-man elimination match (over Chance Charles, Pimp Daddy J, Chris Douglas, and Tommy Grayson) and was named the first EWA North American Cyber Champion by VP Artful.
note: The earliest-recorded North American title reign in this run, predating the previously-transcribed 'first' reign by nearly three months. How the title passed from Chambers to Lonewolf is not accounted for anywhere in this run's surviving record — the gap stands undocumented; Chambers's own reign carries no recorded loss.

title: ewa-1998-north-american
label: "The Extreme One" Tommy Grayson

won.source: Not shown in this run's surviving record — Grayson is already billed as North American Cyber Champion entering wnw-7 (15 July 1998), defending against Wayne Rothschild; his own title win over Connor Chambers (the previously-recorded holder as of 17 June) is not captured.

how: Unrecorded — first appears as champion at wnw-7, retaining there against Wayne "The Train" Rothschild in a Barb Wire Death Match via Showstopper.
note: Bridges the gap between Connor Chambers's recorded win and this run's own previously-first-recorded reign — the actual title change from Chambers to Grayson is not captured anywhere in the surviving record, nor is Grayson's own loss to Lonewolf; both gaps stand undocumented rather than guessed.

end.source: The document's own text — President Artful strips Wayne Rothschild of the title on-air after he fails to appear for a scheduled defense, per the 13 October 1998 Extreme Tonight.
